result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_asymmetric_node_pairs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count asymmetric node pairs (one-way edges) in directed graphs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14439-L14507){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_asymmetric_node_pairs() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Count asymmetric node pairs](/assets/graphs/count-asymmetric-node-pairs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared graph, directed. The one-way edges A to C, B to C, and B to D are in the accent color; the reciprocal pairs between A and B and between C and D are faded. The card counts the three one-way pairs." width="100%"} Returns the number of node pairs `(a,b)` where edge `a->b` exists but not `b->a`. Parallel edges in the same direction are collapsed first, so three `A->C` edges still count as one asymmetric pair. Self-loops are excluded. Together with `count_mutual_node_pairs()`, this describes the dyads of a directed network: every pair of nodes is either mutual, asymmetric (one-way), or unconnected. One-way ties reveal direction, flow, and hierarchy, which makes this count useful for: - spotting status or dominance structure (e.g. who follows whom without being followed back) - measuring how hierarchical a citation, reporting, or food-web network is - computing reciprocity as `mutual / (mutual + asymmetric)` The count covers the whole graph and ignores the current selection. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of node pairs with edges in only one direction. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} This is the complement of `count_mutual_node_pairs()`: here `A -> C` is the only edge without a matching reverse edge, so it's the only pair counted: ::: {#6869497a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "A"), # mutual, not counted ("A", "C"), # asymmetric ] ) ) graph.count_asymmetric_node_pairs() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: A strict hierarchy has no reciprocated ties at all. In this small reporting chain every edge points one way, so each of the three edges is its own asymmetric pair and the mutual count is zero: ::: {#42686561 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} org = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["CEO", "VP1", "VP2", "Mgr"]) .add_edges([("CEO", "VP1"), ("CEO", "VP2"), ("VP1", "Mgr")]) ) org.count_asymmetric_node_pairs(), org.count_mutual_node_pairs() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 0) ``` ::: :::
